coverage.method: units matched across all four source kinds (NCERT_SECTION, NCERT_SUBSECTION, SCOPE_FRAGMENT, CBSE_ONLY) against every identifier an authored artifact carries

methodCorrection.cause: the matcher read only source.section and source.cbseEntry; 22 units are NCERT_SUBSECTION and 9 are SCOPE_FRAGMENT, whose keys live under different fields, so their keys came out blank
methodCorrection.note: the 34 figure was never reported as a finding

finding1.originalFraming: nine units at OPTIONAL_ENRICHMENT contradict the checkpoint-94 policy
finding1.newFact: six of the nine are ALREADY AUTHORED and shipped
finding1.consequence: the debt is mostly a STATUS-LABEL question, not an authoring gap: reclassifying the six would change metadata and counting only, with no new content. Only three would require authoring.

finding2.issue: three units are CBSE_ONLY with ncertChapterOwner null in the decomposition, but their authored artifacts declare an NCERT chapter owner
finding2.whyItMatters: this is the exact error C11-INQ-FO6 was protected from at checkpoints 94 and 96C — a CBSE-only topic given a bibliographic chapter it does not belong to. These three predate that policy.
finding2.whyNot: scope fragments are parts of real NCERT sections, so chapter ownership is correct for them
finding2.impactIfRepaired: would move up to three lessons out of chapter-owned into chapter-less, changing 85/1/1/87 and three chapter row counts

milestone.supported: all 14 current NCERT Class 11 textbook chapters have authored summative-core coverage

order: 1. Decide GD-2 first: ownership is bibliographic truth, and it changes the denominators every later count depends on
2. Then decide GD-1's status question for the six already-authored units — metadata only, no content
3. Only then author FO8, FO10, FO11, if the policy decision makes them required
recommendation.rationale: authoring three lessons before settling the status policy would repeat the FO-6 sequence backwards: content first, governance after
